newsitem.title: USA: Albright exhorts women graduates to persevere.
newsitem.headline: Albright exhorts women graduates to persevere.

text.p: The first U.S. female secretary of state Sunday told graduates of a prestigious women's college they must persevere in their dreams and goals no matter what obstacles confront them, and issued them a call to action.

"There is no doubt, if you aim high enough, that you will be confronted by those who say that your efforts to change the world or to improve the lot of those around you do not mean much in the grand scheme of things," Madeleine Albright said in the commencement address at Mount Holyoke College.

"But no matter how impotent you may sometimes feel, have the courage still -- and persevere," said the 60-year-woman who made history when President Clinton named her America's top diplomat, a post she assumed last January.

She also warned the more than 500 graduates that if they aimed high enough they would find their "strongest beliefs ridiculed and challenged" or "derisively dismissed" and that demands of family, friends and employment "will conspire to distract you from your course."

But Albright, who raised three daughters, learned Russian during baby feedings and laboured long in the political vineyards before serving as U.N. ambassador and then secretary of state, exhorted the class on 1997 to "have courage still -- and persevere."
With the enormous advances in the status of women in recent years, "we could now lower our voices and -- as some suggest -- sit sedately down," she said.
Instead, "we are ready to claim our rightful place as full citizens and full participants in every society on Earth," she urged, drawing cheers and applause from the graduates.

Albright also praised the "uncommon women in all corners of the globe (who) have in common a determination to chart their own path and by doing so to alter for the better the course of their country or community."

She made special mention of women she had met in recent years, including those in Sarajevo "weighted down by personal grief reaching out across ethnic lines to rebuild their shattered society," and in Burundi "taking the lead in efforts to avoid the (genocidal) fate of neigboring Rwanda."

Also, women in Guatemala striving to ensure a new peace is accompanied by justice and in Burma, democracy activist Aung San Suu Kyi "who risks her life every day to keep alive the hope for democracy in her country."

Graduates gave Albright a standing ovation as she received an honorary doctor of laws degree from Mount Holyoke, which produced the first female presidential cabinet member, Frances Perkins, secretary of labour under President Franklin Delano Roosevelt.

Recipient of an undergraduate degree from nearby Wellesley College, another ivy league women's school, Albright was praised during the ceremony as the "embodiment of the women's college graduate -- confounding everyone by doing it all ... You made history by excelling in a male-dominated world."

After the commencement address, Albright flew to Paris where she was to meet French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette on Monday and attend with President Clinton Tuesday's signing of the NATO-Russia agreement setting out terms for their relationship after alliance expansion.
She will also attend a U.S.-European Union summit in The Hague, then visit the Balkans as part of an administration push to revive the troubled Bosnia peace agreement.
